title: $\mathcal{PT}$ and anti-$\mathcal{PT}$ phase transitions in a trimerized Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with nonreciprocal Rashba spin-orbit coupling
authors: Milad Jangjan, Linhu Li, Longwen Zhou, Mir Vahid Hosseini
abstract: We theoretically investigate a one-dimensional trimerized Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with three sublattices per unit cell subjected to a nonreciprocal Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Invoking a spin-flip symmetry, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian decomposes into two independent spin sectors, enabling a spin-resolved analysis of non-Hermitian skin effects and system symmetries. We identify a rich phase diagram consisting of four bulk phases and two edge-state phases. The bulk phases include fully $\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (real-spectrum) and fully anti-$\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (imaginary-spectrum) regimes, as well as two mixed phases where one band remains on the real or imaginary axis while the other two form complex-conjugate pairs. The two edge-state phases correspond to topological edge modes with either $\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (real) or anti-$\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken (imaginary) energies. Using non-Bloch band theory and Cardano's method, we derive closed-form expressions for phase boundaries and establish the bulk-edge correspondence for each spin sector. Calculations of Berry phase and directional inverse participation ratios confirm our analytical predictions. Our results provide a minimal platform for realizing spin-resolved non-Hermitian topology and edge-selective symmetry preservation, in which the bulk and edge states belong to distinct symmetry classes.
summary: This theoretical study investigates non-Hermitian topology in a trimerized SSH chain incorporating nonreciprocal Rashba SOC. By exploiting spin-flip symmetry, the authors map out a complex phase diagram characterized by $\mathcal{PT}$ and anti-$\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry transitions. The work successfully establishes a bulk-edge correspondence, showing how symmetry dictates whether edge states possess real or imaginary energies.
main_problem: The paper investigates $\mathcal{PT}$ and anti-$\mathcal{PT}$ phase transitions in a specific quantum system, focusing on spin-resolved non-Hermitian topology and edge-selective symmetry preservation.
main_result: The system exhibits a rich phase diagram with distinct bulk and edge-state phases, demonstrating spin-dependent non-Hermitian skin effects and the separation of symmetry classes between bulk and edge states.
method: The analysis employs non-Bloch band theory and Cardano's method to derive closed-form expressions for phase boundaries, confirming results using Berry phase and directional inverse participation ratios.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional trimerized Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) chain with three sublattices per unit cell, subjected to a nonreciprocal Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The Hamiltonian is decomposed into two independent spin sectors due to a preserved spin-flip symmetry.
key_observables: Bulk and edge energy spectra (real/imaginary), Berry phase, directional inverse participation ratios, and the classification of phases (e.g., $\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken, anti-$\mathcal{PT}$-unbroken).
important_parameters: Intracell ($t$) and intercell ($t'$) hopping amplitudes, dimerization strength ($\delta t$), and nonreciprocal Rashba coupling ($\lambda, \lambda'$ with $\delta\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a spin-flip symmetry, which allows the Hamiltonian to be block-diagonalized into two independent spin sectors.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the $\text{SSH}3$ lattice couplings. Figure 2 (mentioned) shows the phase diagram in the $(\delta t, \delta \lambda)$ plane for both spin sectors.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the Hamiltonian and exploiting the spin-flip symmetry to decompose the problem. It then uses non-Bloch theory to analyze the bulk spectrum via a cubic secular equation, followed by edge state analysis to establish the bulk-edge correspondence for different symmetry regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends the study of topological phases into the non-Hermitian domain, specifically addressing how $\mathcal{PT}$ and anti-$\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries dictate the nature of edge states in complex lattice models.
